proposals.evidence: DEDR 2053 attests Tamil koṭu, Malayalam koṭukka, Kannada koḍu/kuḍu and Kodagu koḍï give. The survey simple verbs belong to this stem; give-away compounds and the separate tā-/ī- giving stems are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 4410 explicitly attests Tamil/Malayalam pēr, Kota pēr, Telugu pēru, Gadaba/Parji pidir, Gondi peder/porol, Tulu pudaru and Konda/Kuvi dōru name. The selected simple name nouns fit these branches; Indo-Aryan nām forms and potentially contact-mediated Kannada pēru are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 4885 directly groups the mīn fish series in Kannada, Kodagu, Kota, Tamil, Tulu and Malto (mínu). The survey final -ə and Malto -du are retained. Badaga and Ravula are comparative extensions explicitly labelled look-alikes by the upstream annotation; neither is falsely described as listed in DEDR. The article’s Sanskrit mīna comparison does not itself specify a loan route for these records. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 2115 directly gives Kodagu kombï and Tamil/Malayalam kompu horn. The source survey kombə/kompə spellings preserve final-vowel and voicing differences. Badaga, Betta Kurumba and Ravula forms are comparative extensions of this distinctive nasal-stop stem, explicitly only look-alikes in the upstream annotation, pending inheritance/contact review. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
